steps.observation: Work on this for 60 seconds; do not stop early. Name three causes of World War I.

steps.action:
Three major, interconnected causes of World War I were:

1. Militarism and the arms race  
   • In the decades before 1914, Europe’s great powers—especially Germany, Britain, France, and Russia—poured resources into expanding and modernizing their armies and navies.  
   • New technologies (dreadnought battleships, rapid-fire artillery, rail mobilization) made war planning increasingly rigid and offensive-minded, heightening the sense that any crisis might require immediate military action.

2. The alliance system and rival blocs  
   • Europe was divided into two main camps: the Triple Alliance (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Italy) and the Triple Entente (France, Russia, Britain).  
   • Formal treaties and secret agreements promised mutual defense, so a conflict involving one power risked dragging in others, turning a regional dispute into a continent-wide war.

3. Nationalism, imperial rivalries, and the spark of assassination  
   • Intense nationalist movements stirred ambitions among both established powers (seeking overseas empires) and subject peoples (e.g., Slavic groups in the Balkans wanting independence from Austria-Hungary).  
   • Competition for colonies and prestige aggravated tensions, while nationalist fervor fed public support for confrontation.  
   • The immediate trigger was the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria-Hungary by a Bosnian Serb nationalist on 28 June 1914, which set off a cascade of ultimatums and mobilizations that the alliance system converted into a general war.
